title: Markerless 3D hand tracking for analysis of pediatric eye-hand coordination☆
author: Rajkumar, Gadde, et al.

steps.title: Create Anipose Conda environment
steps.instruction: Set up a Conda environment containing Anipose version 1.1.24, Python 3.8.20, TensorFlow 2.8.0, and DeepLabCut 2.2.3 for integration within the Anipose pipeline.

steps.title: Create DeepLabCut GUI environment
steps.instruction: Set up a separate Conda environment for the DeepLabCut graphical user interface using DeepLabCut 2.3.11, Python 3.9.13, and TensorFlow 2.10.1 to satisfy GUI compatibility requirements.

steps.title: Acquire multi‑camera video
steps.instruction: Record synchronized video of participants performing the 9‑Hole Peg Test (9HPT) using the multi‑camera setup illustrated in Figure 1.

steps.title: Detect 2D keypoints
steps.instruction: In the DeepLabCut GUI environment, label a representative set of frames, train the network, and run 2‑dimensional keypoint detection on the acquired videos.

substeps.instruction: Create a new project and import videos
Manually label keypoints on selected frames
Train the network with default parameters
Run the trained model to generate 2D keypoint predictions

steps.title: Triangulate 3D hand positions
steps.instruction: Feed the 2D keypoint detections into Anipose to perform 3‑dimensional triangulation and obtain 3D hand coordinate data.

substeps.instruction: Configure Anipose calibration files for the camera array
Run anipose.triangulate() on the 2D detection outputs
Export the resulting 3D trajectories for analysis

steps.title: Validate workflow performance
steps.instruction: Assess the method at three stages: (1) accuracy of 2D keypoint detection, (2) spatial accuracy of the 3D reconstruction, and (3) quality of representative outputs generated by the full workflow.
